architecture.title: The P4 architecture
architecture.summary: A through-the-road P4. The stock front powerpack stays exactly as delivered, and the team replaces the rear mechanical differential with a team-designed electric drive unit fed by a team-built pack in the rear hatch. There is no mechanical connection between the two axles - the road is the coupling. Every constraint below follows from that one sentence.
architecture.source: Kickoff Competition Technical Slides, VHI high-level program constraints
in_scope: Collect baseline data with the stock vehicle
Designing and integrating the P4 drive unit - motor, inverter, gearbox - to replace the stock rear mechanical differential
Static linear finite element analysis on any structural modification
Balancing efficiency and performance attributes, off-road included
permitted: Different springs and dampers, including active suspension
Enhanced thermal or electrical modelling and simulation
Declared use of hardware from previous university projects
Driving on public roads with university approval
A standalone thermal system for the team EDU or battery pack
prohibited: Stock thermal or refrigerant system changes
Battery integration outside the defined area in the rear hatch
architecture.callout: Declared use of hardware from previous university projects sits in the permitted, likely not scored column. Prior Battery Workforce Challenge hardware is therefore usable only if it is declared, it earns no points, and it must never appear in a submission as new EcoCAR work.
